newsitem.title: UK: Wall St leads Eurobourses higher, dlr sags.
newsitem.headline: Wall St leads Eurobourses higher, dlr sags.

text.p: European shares returned to their winning ways on Monday after Wall Street moved higher shortly after it opened for business, but the dollar slid against the mark.
"Wall Street has been giving us a helping hand and as long as it holds up there's no reason why we won't keep going higher," one dealer in London said.

Wall Street's Dow Jones index of leading shares, which rose 56 points on Friday, was up more than 25 points at 7,025.9 by 1545 gmt, when London's FTSE index was up 12.9 points at 4,433 and France's CAC-40 index was up 1.85 points at 2,710.13, though both were off their day's best levels. German shares had already closed at a new record.

The markets on both sides of the Atlantic were encouraged by the U.S. jobs report for February which on Friday showed little upward pressure on wages, despite a bigger-than-expected rise in the number of new jobs created.
Economists and traders concluded that the jobs report had not given the U.S. Federal Reserve cause to raise interest rates soon to check the threat of inflation.
Any rise in rates could sorely test the global bull market in shares which has pushed valuations to record after record recently.
Investors in shares fear higher interest rates as they harm companies profitability by rising the cost of borrowing. They also make alternative investments more attractive.
Leading London blue chips shares moved further into record territory, lifted by bullish comments from the Bank of England as well as Wall Street, dealers said.
Gilts also advanced after Bank of England Governor Eddie George said he believed the government could reach its 2.5 percent inflation target this year.

"He raised the question about whether it could be sustained, but up until now, he didn't even think it was a target that could be reached," one London share dealer said of George's forecast. "I think the chance of an early rate increase has receded quite significantly."
British February producer price inflation was in line with expectations at 1.3 percent and one analyst said the data showed inflation was "very tame at the moment."

French shares were showing a small gains by midafternoon, having been much firmer durung the morning when non-domestic buying from cash-rich funds saw prices bounce off a springboard of support around the 2,700 level, traders said.
"Foreigners have lots of cash that they want to invest. It's a state of mind. The French are staying out of it," a Paris share trader said earlier.
Germany's blue-chip DAX index ended bourse trade at a new closing high with sentiment lifted by Friday's strong close on Wall Street above 7,000 points, firmer debt and a stable, if lower, dollar.
At the end of the floor-trade session the DAX index stood at 3,436.07 points, up 59.87 points or 1.77 percent, an all-time closing high for the index.

The DAX index was also playing catch-up with its IBIS counterpart, which opened at 3,416.99 points, and rose as high as 3,442.06 points during the morning, though it had fallen back to 3,427.86 by midafternoon.
Among the main gainers on Monday was engineering group Deutz AG, which was continuing to enjoy positive sentiment after reports last week that the group would report a profit next year.
Monday was also the opening day for trade in Frankfurt's new market for technology, new media and other growth stocks, the Neue Markt, modelled on New York's Nasdaq index.

The initial public offering in shares in German mobile phone service provider Mobilcom AG, which will trade on the Neue Markt, were more than 100 times oversubscribed, its chief executive Gerhard Schmid told Reuters on Monday.
In currencies, the dollar was lower, weakened by profit-taking after its brief rise above 1.72 marks last week, and covering of mark shorts, traders said.
Against the backdrop of a firmer mark the dollar slipped close to the 1.70 mark level after erosion of support at 1.7050 triggered stop-loss selling.

"We have seen somewhat of a recovery in the mark in the past few days and that is continuing gently," said Paul Crowhurst, a trader at Bank of Boston in London. "The dollar is still consolidating because it had come a long way quite quickly but the retracement is not very large."
At 1545 GMT, the dollar was trading at 1.7032 compared with 1.7182 late on Friday. The dollar was trading at 121.65 against the yen, also weaker.
CURRENCIES AT 1545 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.7032 marks and 121.65 yen compared with 1.7182 marks and 121.94 yen in late European trade on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS 1545 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 12.9 points at 4,433.2.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 1.85 points at 2,710.13.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 59.87 points at 3,436.07 points.
PRECIOUS METALS AT 1545 GMT

Gold fixed at $350.90 an ounce in the afternoon in London compared with $349.05 at the European close on Friday. The market was physically steadier but no direction had emerged since last week's fall on Swiss sales news.
